clue.text: A way of imagining a bit on the side?

definitions.text: A way of imagining a bit on the side?

parts.words: A way of imagining a bit on the side?
parts.note: a bit on the side reads as an affair, but a way of thinking that comes at a problem sideways, from an unexpected angle, is meant

explanation.surface: A coy question about fantasising over an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit on the side' is British slang for an illicit lover; here 'on the side' instead means sideways, a creative approach to problems.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the creative, sideways problem-solving style popularised by Edward de Bono.

clue.text: Look feasible without one inspiring devotion

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look

indicators.note: without tells us the word for feasible loses the letter for one

parts.note: something feasible is viable
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A plan that looks workable without anyone being devoted to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lovable is easy to adore, so they inspire devotion; a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Detect a serviceman's concealed weapon

indicators.note: concealed says the weapon lies tucked away inside the run of words Detect a serviceman's

explanation.surface: Security spots a weapon hidden on a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'detecT A SERviceman's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electric stun gun, a type of weapon.

clue.text: Outfit with morale destroyed in complicated procedures

parts.note: a rig is an outfit of clothing or equipment

indicators.note: destroyed says the letters of morale are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Dressing up for some convoluted bureaucracy leaves everyone's spirits shattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outfit' reads as a verb but is a noun, the clothing or kit; 'destroyed' scrambles MORALE to AMROLE, and 'with' and 'in' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, fussy, complicated process or set of formalities.

clue.text: Attack yobbo hugging tree

indicators.note: hugging means the word for yobbo wraps its arms around the tree word

parts.note: a yobbo is British slang for a lout, a rough young man
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A thug clutching a tree trunk before lunging at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yobbo' is British slang for a loutish hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out is to suddenly attack someone physically or verbally; a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Tool cuts a cow's tail

parts.note: hacks means chops or cuts roughly

indicators.note: tail picks out the last letter of the word cow's

explanation.surface: A tool used to chop off a cow's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw used for cutting metal, a workshop tool.

clue.text: Country gentlemen take up opera and travel, finally

indicators.note: finally applies to every word around it here, taking the closing letter of each of gentlemen, take, up, opera and travel

explanation.surface: Wealthy gents acquire a taste for opera and travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country gentlemen' looks like a phrase, but 'Country' alone is the definition; 'and' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan nation lying between India and China.

clue.text: Trouble with a flirt makes you uncomfortable

parts.note: ill as a noun means harm or trouble
a tease is someone who flirts and leads others on

explanation.surface: Getting entangled with a flirt can leave you awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill at ease is an idiom for feeling awkward or uncomfortable.

clue.text: Channels good for money in golf clubs?

indicators.note: good for money means the letter for good takes the place of the letter for money

parts.note: putters are golf clubs used on the green
P stands for penny, a unit of money

explanation.surface: A question whether channels for cash flow through golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good for money' puts G in place of P (penny) in PUTTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutters are channels that carry rainwater along roofs or roadsides.

clue.text: Faces drop during struggles

indicators.note: during means the drop word occurs within the struggles word

parts.note: vies means competes or struggles
sag means droop or drop

explanation.surface: Expressions fall in the middle of a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Visages are faces, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Company scheme adopting single high-flier

indicators.note: adopting means the scheme word takes the single letter into itself

parts.note: a plot is a scheme
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for single

explanation.surface: A firm's plan to take on one ambitious executive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flier' suggests a go-getter but literally means someone flying an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-pilot flies a plane alongside the captain, so literally flies high.

clue.text: Cruel gibe — almost cause excitement

parts.note: a barb is a cutting remark or gibe

indicators.note: almost means the phrase for cause excitement is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to arouse is to cause excitement

explanation.surface: A cutting taunt that nearly stirs things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarous means savagely cruel or brutal, a synonym.

clue.text: Turner departed around the end of March

indicators.note: around means the departed word goes round the other piece

parts.note: late can mean dead, departed

indicators.note: the end of selects the closing letter of March

explanation.surface: The painter Turner died towards the end of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the painter J M W Turner, but it is a machine that turns wood or metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine that turns material while it is shaped, so it is a turner.

clue.text: Furthest goal confronting the majority

indicators.note: confronting means the goal word stands facing, so ahead of, the majority word

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
most means the majority

explanation.surface: A distant target facing up to most people.
explanation.definitionFit: Endmost means furthest along or nearest the end, a synonym.

clue.text: Takeaways that might spoil the canines?

definitions.text: Takeaways that might spoil the canines?

parts.words: Takeaways that might spoil the canines?
parts.note: leftovers carried home from a restaurant, supposedly for the pet dogs, who would be spoilt by the treat

explanation.surface: Wondering if leftover meals would pamper the dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: Takeaways here are leftovers taken from a restaurant, nominally for the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The bags diners use to carry home uneaten food, pretending it is for the dog.

clue.text: Sixty per cent of women — crazy for animals!

indicators.note: sixty per cent of a five-letter word is its first three letters, here of women

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: An exclamation that most women are mad about animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Three of the five letters of WOMEN is 60%, giving WOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Wombats are burrowing Australian marsupials, examples of animals.

clue.text: Herald compiler on ship turning green!

parts.note: the compiler, the setter, refers to themselves as me
SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: turning signals the letters of green twisting into another order

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter aboard a vessel goes green with seasickness.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter calling themselves 'me' is a common crossword convention; 'turning' twists GREEN into ENGER, and 'on' simply links.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald carries news or announcements, as a messenger does.

clue.text: Pay no attention to gentle rocking around front of car

indicators.note: around means the shaken letters wrap round the next piece
rocking shakes the letters of gentle into a new order
front of takes the first letter of car

explanation.surface: Ignoring someone soothingly rocking near a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocking' makes NEGLET from GENTLE, which goes around C.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to fail to attend to it, an exact verb synonym.

clue.text: Unsettled comedian is worried, lacking energy

indicators.note: is worried means the letters of comedian are troubled into a fresh order, with lacking saying one letter drops out

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A nervous comic, drained of energy, is out of sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: COMEDIAN rearranged without its E gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic peoples wander without a fixed home, so they are unsettled.

clue.text: Part of orchestra using tiny amp

indicators.note: using is a loose signal that the letters of tiny amp are employed in a new order

explanation.surface: Some of the orchestra are playing through a small amplifier.
explanation.definitionFit: The tympani, or timpani, are kettledrums in the percussion section of an orchestra.

clue.text: Have search parties started at the beginning?

parts.note: posses are groups gathered to hunt someone down

indicators.note: at the beginning picks out the opening letter of started

explanation.surface: Asking whether the search groups set off at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess is to have or own, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Prior to calculations, regularly spooks animals

indicators.note: Prior to puts the picked letters ahead of the calculations word
regularly takes every other letter of spooks, the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: sums are arithmetic calculations

explanation.surface: Before the sums, ghosts keep turning up among the animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of sPoOkS give POS.
explanation.definitionFit: Possums are small tree-dwelling marsupials, examples of animals.

clue.text: Dancing valkyries dismiss a king with a clear tone

indicators.note: Dancing sets the letters of valkyries whirling into a new order once some are dropped

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Warrior maidens dance, sending away a monarch, in bell-like voices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismiss' signals that A and K leave VALKYRIES before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A silvery sound is clear, light and ringing, like a small bell.

clue.text: Head of city might love reporter's finish

parts.note: may and might both express possibility
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: finish takes the last letter of reporter's

explanation.surface: A civic leader might love how a journalist's piece ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of city' looks like a first-letter signal for C, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayor is the elected head of a city or town council.

clue.text: Path unavailable in case of resistance

indicators.note: in means the unavailable word sits within those outer letters
case of takes the outer letters, the casing, of resistance

parts.note: out means not available, as in out of stock

explanation.surface: A way blocked if the opposition turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a way or path taken from one place to another.

clue.text: Almost complete support for teacher exercising authority

indicators.note: support for means the shortened word props up, so follows, the teacher word

parts.note: a master is a schoolteacher

indicators.note: Almost cuts the final letter from the word for complete

parts.note: full means complete

explanation.surface: A nearly finished back-up for a commanding schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Masterful means commanding and authoritative, so exercising authority.

clue.text: Distress signal emitted by fellow with real trouble

indicators.note: trouble disturbs the letters of real into a new order

explanation.surface: A man in real difficulty sends up a distress signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emitted by' and 'with' are links that make the surface read naturally; 'trouble' turns REAL into LARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A flare is a bright pyrotechnic fired as a distress signal at sea.

clue.text: Joker comes back with shapeless formula for novel

indicators.note: comes back means the joker word is read in reverse

parts.note: a card is a joker or wit

indicators.note: shapeless means a word for shape is removed from formula

explanation.surface: A comedian returns with a vague recipe for a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back' turns CARD into DRAC; 'shapeless' takes FORM (shape) from FORMULA, leaving ULA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dracula is Bram Stoker's 1897 vampire novel.

clue.text: Improve at university level

parts.note: up means at university, as in up at Oxford
a grade is a level or rank

explanation.surface: Raising standards at college level.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a student is 'up' while at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To upgrade something is to improve it to a higher standard.

clue.text: Operating procedure turning customer grey (sic)

indicators.note: turning means the letters of customer, grey and sic are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: An operation that leaves a client looking grey, as noted.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic surgery is an operation done to change appearance, literally an operating procedure.
